Number two, there's no such thing as a viral hook. Hooks perform when they're perfectly crafted to speak to someone's pain points in less than five seconds. items.transcript: How the fuck do you write hooks so good people comment, wow, this video was literally made for me? It's called the triple hook, and if done correctly, it'll paralyze anyone from scrolling. It works in three steps. Miss one, and your whole hook will fall apart. Starting with step one, context. The first line of your hook has to tell the viewer exactly what this video is about, immediately. If they don't know what they're watching in the first second, they're gonna go away. Here's an example. This is not an inclined chest press. Step two, the pull. Once they know what it's about, You need to make them actually want to care. There are four ways to execute this. The first is the taboo pool. Say something that feels slightly uncomfortable or socially dangerous to say out loud. The second is the dark pool. Expose something hidden that the viewer didn't know was actually happening to them. The third is the contradiction pool. Say something that directly contradicts what they already believe to be true. The fourth is the proof pool. Give factual evidence or stats to back up what you're already saying. Pick one, and if you can visually show it, the stronger your pool will be. Step three, the whiplash. Think of it like fishing. You get the hook in the fish's mouth swimming one direction, then you yank the line the other way. The whiplash in layman's terms is stating something completely polar opposite to what people were anticipating what you were going to say. Here's an example. This reel got 2 million views and made zero sales. Here's what I'm doing to never go viral again. So keep this always in mind. A great hook isn't catchy, it's a trap. Context sets it in, the pool loads it, and then the whiplash shuts it. Now if you want to take this a step further, comment story, and I'll send you my YouTube video where I go into more detail on how to write better hooks using your own personal experience.

items.transcript: I gained over 3 million followers in the last 12 months for my clients, so I figured I'd tell you exactly what I did for them so you could steal it for yourself. First, there's three things that you should not be doing. Fuck posting three times a day. I recommend five to six times a week max. Second, a posting schedule. You don't need a specific type of post on a specific type of day. That's stupid. Third, you're not going to fall for a specific type of format that you have to do. Yapping. Now here are the five things that you should be focusing on to cut the bullshit so you don't get overwhelmed, actually build authority, stay consistent, and finally start signing some clients. Number one, stop doing everything on the same day, finding ideas, scripting, filming it, and then editing it. You're going to get overwhelmed. You're not going to get anything done. Instead, I'd rather have you do all your ideas in one day, do all your scripting another day, and all your filming another day, and then send your videos to your editor to actually edit it. Number two, stop making your life harder by making one video and you just post on Instagram and call it a day. You can turn it into a carousel. You can turn it into a seven second B-roll video. You can actually refilm it. The list goes on. Don't just make one video and call it a day. Number three, build your characters. So things that you want people to recognize you for. This can be your location, your outfit, things, people, whatever you want people to be like, oh, wait, that's Ayush every single time they see it. Number four, build your core mission and make your content revolve around it. I don't teach how to go viral. I teach you how to actually build authority with your content. And for fun, we go viral. And now number five, this is going to be the biggest game changer for you. Find viral videos outside of your niche, take the framework and apply your core mission to that said framework. This will allow you to be original with your videos and this is how you stand out and become a one of one. Now, trust me, I got more game to give you. So make sure you follow for more value like this.

items.transcript: How the fuck do you steal a video without getting caught? Most of our best performing videos started with an idea someone else already proved. I call it the three digital fingerprints. When you nail all three, your content goes from something that gets watched to something that gets you clients. Step one, understand the mechanism, not just the tactic. The mechanism is a psychology underneath the video. Did they hit a specific pain point their ideal client has? How did they hit it? Through fear, through curiosity, through proof. That's what made the video work. Not the hook, not the format, the emotional trigger underneath it. Step two, find your angle. Take the validated idea and see what you can add on to the existing information. What do you believe about this topic that nobody else is saying? What have you seen in your own experience that contradicts the common advice? Step three, make it impossible for someone to copy you. Your format, your client stories, your personal experience, your personality. Nobody else has the exact combination of these, so use even one of them and the video becomes yours. Founders who copy without understanding why, they stay invisible to their ideal clients. The digital fingerprint fixes all of that. Understand the mechanism, find your angle, and make it impossible to be copied. Your content will go from a cover band to the only voice in your space your ideal client actually trusts. If your content is getting views, but your audience still doesn't trust you enough to buy, comment onyx and I'll work with you one-on-one to fix your entire content system.
